cover_html:
5 PROMPTS · HEALTH ADMIN
Let Claude read
your medical mail
Visits, bills, denials. Copy, paste, done. Black out your ID numbers first. Swipe ▸
SAMPLE · EXPLANATION OF BENEFITS
OFFICE VISIT $310.00
PLAN PAID $70.00
YOU OWE $240.00
THIS IS NOT A BILL

slides.title: Prep your *visit*
slides.prompt: I have a short doctor visit about [issue]. Turn my notes below into a one page summary: when it started, what helps or makes it worse, the medicines I take, and my top 3 questions.
slides.why: Visits go fast. You walk in organized and leave with answers.

slides.title: Check the *EOB*
slides.prompt: Here is my Explanation of Benefits and the bill from my provider. Check the dates, services and the amount I owe. Do they match? List every difference.
slides.why: An EOB is not a bill. What it says you owe should match the bill. If the bill comes first, wait for the EOB.

slides.title: Audit the *bill*
slides.prompt: Here is my itemized medical bill with my name and ID numbers blacked out. Explain each line in plain words, flag possible duplicates, and list questions for the billing office.
slides.why: Ask the billing office for the itemized bill. A summary bill hides the details.

slides.title: Answer a *denial*
slides.prompt: My insurer denied this claim. Here is the denial letter. Write a short, polite appeal that answers their exact reason and asks for a full review. Leave blanks for my policy numbers.
slides.why: You usually have up to 180 days to appeal. The denial is not the last word.

slides.title: Never miss a *step*
slides.prompt: Here are my visit notes. Turn them into a simple checklist: each medicine and when to take it, follow up dates, and the warning signs that mean I should call the doctor.
slides.why: Notes get lost. A checklist on the fridge does not. Your doctor has the final say.

cta.gift: Your free bill guide: the steps and Claude prompts to cut a medical bill before you pay.
cta.small: Free in your DMs. *Not medical or legal advice.*

bg_facts: An EOB is not a bill.
Compare what you owe on the EOB with the bill.
You usually have up to 180 days to appeal a denied claim.
